page: OVHcloud c3-4 is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a 2.3 GHz base frequency, with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 50 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core execution capabilities, with stress-ng single-core compute scoring 3083.56, placing it in the top 25% tier. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reflect the limitations of the dual-core topology; stress-ng multi-core performance reaches an average score of 6125.55, while Geekbench multi-core (3412.0) and Clang software compilation (4141.0) fall into the bottom 25%. Memory throughput remains moderate, reaching 61.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 29.93 GB/sec for writes. PassMark CPU (5442.44) and memory (1378.22) tests place in the lower quartile, and static web serving throughput measures at 2.57 GB/sec.

From a qualitative efficiency perspective, the c3-4 offers dedicated compute execution without hyperthread sharing, providing consistent CPU cycles at an entry-level resource scale. However, the 4.0 GB memory envelope and dual-core boundary restrict its ability to process memory-intensive or highly parallelized workloads. The instance is suited for lightweight computational services, dedicated background worker nodes, small-scale batch data processing, and internal development or testing environments.
description: OVHcloud c3-4 is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors operating at 2.3 GHz. The configuration provides 2 dedicated physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory profile alongside 50 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark metrics show strong single-core performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the upper quartile, coupled with mid-tier large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression throughput. Overall multi-core throughput and PassMark scores remain lower due to the dual-core constraint, and static web serving measures 2.57 GB/sec. Featuring hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI with no bundled GPUs, OVHcloud c3-4 is well suited for dedicated microservices, lightweight batch jobs, utility tooling, and non-parallelized compute tasks requiring dedicated physical CPU allocation.
